title: Knockout, fairness, and commercial drafting
summary: The notes juxtapose the Code’s default terms with firms’ strategies for avoiding unwanted boilerplate.
notes:
Casebook discussion of a shorter authority.

Gardner Zemke’s discussion addresses situations in which the parties’ conduct cannot identify a negotiated common term. Keating’s empirical discussion distinguishes imposing one’s own terms from avoiding the other side’s terms. The editors preserve arguments that warranty defaults protect buyers and arguments that those defaults encourage sellers’ drafting strategies. Neither perspective is encoded as a judicial holding of Northrop.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 292–294. Open assigned page 292.
